_meta.description: Which CivicGraph data objects evidence each ACT project. Declared FROM THE PROJECT SIDE: the claim 'these tables evidence Goods' is a statement about the work, so it lives here under version control next to project-codes.json, and is mirrored onto CivicGraph's clarity_object.project_codes for fast filtering (same edge, stored once, written from the end that owns the meaning).
rules: Keys must be codes from project-codes.json; values are CivicGraph clarity_object object_keys.

Declare only what you can defend — a wrong declaration pollutes the zero-evidence report, which is the metric this file exists to make honest: of 74 project codes, how many can the data not speak about at all?

Mirror with: node --env-file=.env scripts/sync-project-evidence.mjs (run from the grantscope repo). The sync validates both ends and refuses unknown codes or unknown objects rather than skipping them silently.

The optional 'repos' map declares each code's primary codebase (a directory name under ~/Code on the machine running the sync). Repo freshness is MEASURED at sync time, never declared. Declare only repos you are sure of — a wrong repo link makes a dormant project look alive.
